14	CASE OD2-HO-CONFOUND-2 (CONFOUND, technical): The crashing canvas flag

18	E1 [stage S1] Crash dashboard export, Quillmark Android, panel 'Crash-affected sessions by flag cohort' (telemetry): Period 10–16 Sep 2026. Overall daily crash-affected sessions: 1 Sep 0.70%, 4 Sep 0.74%, 7 Sep 0.83%, 9 Sep 0.92%, 12 Sep 0.99%, 16 Sep 1.01%. Annotation added by the dashboard owner: 'Flag ramp 10% (4 Sep) → 50% (7 Sep) → 90% (10 Sep). Curve follows the ramp.' The panel has no filter or breakdown for app version or device.

'The numbers could not be clearer: people with Tiled Canvas crash nearly three times as often as everyone else, and the overall rate climbed step for step with the ramp. Changes in 7.4.0: (1) Tiled Canvas client code, which stays inactive unless the tiled_canvas flag is on; (2) image library Pixelda upgraded from 2.8 to 3.1 to support HEIF photo attachments; (3) Tracewell crash-reporting SDK upgraded from 4.9 to 5.0, which adds capture of native (C/C++) crashes; (4) notification channel cleanup; (5) translation updates.

22	E5 [stage S1] Incident channel #inc-crash-rate, excerpt, 15 Sep (staff-account): Dev (SRE): 'sync-service deployed on 9 Sep around 14:00 UTC, and the overall crash curve gets steeper around then. Tomás (PM): 'Also remember who ends up with the flag in practice. Our heaviest sketchers update first, and heavy users always crash more.' Nobody in the thread posted figures broken down by app version, device or usage.
23	CATALOGUE (full contents)
24	C1 [stage S1] Crash-affected session rates by app version, flag state and device memory tier, daily, 1–16 Sep - Product analytics query by data analyst Ines Waldmark (telemetry): Crash-affected sessions as recorded by Tracewell. 7.3.2 (no flag possible): 0.68–0.72% daily 1–16 Sep, unchanged after 9 Sep. 7.4.0: 1.93–2.12% daily from 2 Sep, including 1.99% on 2–3 Sep, before the flag ramp. 7.4.0, 10–16 Sep: flag on 2.10%, random flag-off holdout 1.98% (difference +0.12 points, user-clustered 95% interval −0.08 to +0.32). 25	C2 [stage S1] Top crash clusters for builds 7.3.2 and 7.4.0, with app-store console crash statistics, 10–16 Sep - Tracewell console export and app-store developer console, pulled by release engineer (log): Tracewell, 7.4.0, top clusters by event count. #1: SIGSEGV in libpixelda.so pd_decode_heif_tile on thread pixelda-worker-*, 41% of events. Photo attachments placed on a canvas are decoded through the shared image pipeline (Pixelda) and cached as tiles; the classic note viewer uses the same pipeline. 30	C7 [stage S1] Tiled Canvas pre-launch QA report, 28 Aug - QA team (document): Tested on 14 device models (3 of them with 3 GB RAM) using internal build 7.4.0-rc2 with the flag forced on. 212 scripted test cases, with no crashes in scripted runs. 31	C8 [stage S1] Interview with the Tiled Canvas tech lead, 16 Sep - Interview notes (staff-account): 'Our code didn't change between the 10% and 90% steps, and our own logging shows no exceptions in the tile renderer. 32	C9 [stage S1] Device model and OS version distribution of all weekly active users, September - Product analytics standard report (telemetry): The top 10 device models account for 34% of users. 32% of sessions run on devices with 4 GB RAM or less. 71% of users are on OS version 13 or newer. Median device age is 2.6 years. The report covers all users combined and is not split by app version, flag state or crash outcome.
33	C10 [stage S1] Flag service audit log for tiled_canvas, 20 Aug–16 Sep - Flag service (system-record): 20 Aug: flag created by canvas-team with the eligibility rule and a 10% holdout. 4 Sep 09:12: rollout 0→10% (approved by J. Arkwright). 7 Sep 10:40: 10→50%. 10 Sep 09:05: 50→90%. 15 Sep 16:20: rollout frozen by M. Edevane. No changes to the eligibility rule, bucketing or holdout since the flag was created.
34	C11 [stage S1] Tracewell SDK 5.0 vendor release notes and migration guide - Tracewell (crash-reporting vendor) (vendor-account): 'Version 5.0 adds native crash capture for C/C++ libraries and improves de-duplication. 35	C12 [stage S1] Tiled Canvas engagement metrics for flagged users, 4–16 Sep - Canvas team analytics dashboard (telemetry): Canvas opens per flagged user per day: 1.4 (the same users with the old canvas in August: 1.3). 36	C13 [stage S1] Postmortem of the March 2025 'Quick Share' crash spike - Engineering wiki (prior-report): In March 2025, a flag-gated share sheet crashed on one OS version. Turning the flag off brought crash rates back to baseline within a day. Recorded lesson: 'When a flag cohort's crash rate jumps, turn the flag off first and investigate after.' Author: M. Edevane. Follow-up actions were all marked closed in May 2025.
37	C14 [stage S1] 7.4.0 beta channel crash statistics, 12–31 Aug - Beta programme report (telemetry): Beta users (n = 8,900) on 7.4.0-beta2 had 1.6% crash-affected sessions, compared with 1.1% for 7.3.2-beta in July. Report author: 'Beta crash rates usually run higher than production.'
38	C15 [stage S1] Lab memory profile of Tiled Canvas and the old canvas on a 3 GB test device - Performance lab, QA team (independent-observation): Scripted 20-minute sketch session with the same content, both conditions on 7.4.0. Peak app memory: old canvas 268 MB, Tiled Canvas 404 MB. In a 10-app switching loop, the app was killed in the background in 1 of 10 runs with the old canvas and 3 of 10 runs with Tiled Canvas. Engineer's note: 'Small sample. It suggests more background kills on low-RAM devices, but it doesn't tell us how often that happens in the field.'

40	H1: Code that runs only when the Tiled Canvas flag is on is the source of the crash-rate gap between flagged and unflagged users.
41	H2: Flagged users are all on the 7.4.0 build, and a change in that build other than the flag's code is the source of the crash-rate gap.
42	H3: Flagged users are concentrated on lower-memory or older devices, and that device mix, not the flag's code, is the source of the crash-rate gap.
43	H4: The crash-rate gap is a counting artifact of the updated crash-reporting SDK rather than a real difference in crashes.
44	H5: Flagged users use the app more heavily than unflagged users, and that usage pattern, not the flag's code, is the source of the crash-rate gap.
45	R1: Tiled Canvas flag enabled for a user -> Higher crash-affected session rate for that user (causes)
46	R2: User running build 7.4.0 -> Higher crash-affected session rate for that user (causes)
47	R3: User running build 7.4.0 -> User eligible to receive the Tiled Canvas flag (determines)
48	R4: Sync-service backend deployment on 9 September -> Higher crash-affected session rate (causes)

50	A2: Hold the 7.4.0 staged rollout at its current 25% and prioritise a fix build for 7.4.0's leading crash clusters before any further rollout.
51	A3: Require the canvas team to rework Tiled Canvas's tile memory handling before the flag ramp is allowed to continue.
52	A4: Widen the random flag-off holdout among 7.4.0 users from 10% to 30% for two weeks to measure whether the flag adds memory kills.
53	A5: Roll the crash-reporting SDK back to Tracewell 4.9 in the next build so crash rates are comparable with 7.3.2.

55	Q1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	Q2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
57	Q3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
58	Q4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
59	Q5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

61	Q7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]

63	Q9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]

H5: Flagged users use the app more heavily than unflagged users, and that usage pattern, not the flag's code, is the source of the crash-rate gap.

answers.justification: Within 7.4.0, the random flag-off holdout crashes at 1.98% against 2.10% with the flag on (+0.12, CI −0.08 to +0.32) (C1), and no top cluster contains canvas.tiles frames (C2), so flag code cannot explain the 2.8x gap in E1; at most a small residual effect remains.

7.4.0 crashes at about 2% from 2 Sep, before the flag ramp, against about 0.7% for 7.3.2 (C1); the top 7.4.0 cluster (41%) is a Pixelda 3.1 HEIF SIGSEGV that is absent from 7.3.2 (C2, E3); and the flag is gated to 7.4.0 (E4).
The share of sessions on devices with 4 GB or less is 31% flag on, 30% holdout and 33% on 7.3.2, and the 7.4.0 vs 7.3.2 gap persists within each memory tier (C1).

The independent app-store console shows the same gap, 2.04% vs 0.69% (Tracewell 2.09% vs 0.70%), and lists libpixelda.so as first seen 2 Sep (C2), so the gap is not just new native-crash capture by Tracewell 5.0 (C11).
Weekly sessions per user (12.3/12.2/12.3) and median session length (6.1/6.0/5.8 min) are essentially the same for flag on, holdout and 7.3.2 (C1), which rules out the heavy-user explanation in E5.

The raw association is large (E1), but in the randomized holdout the effect is small and not significant (+0.12, CI −0.08 to +0.32; memory kills likewise, C1), while a plausible memory mechanism remains (C4, C15), so causation is not established.

The rise starts with 7.4.0 on 2 Sep (C1); the build is offered to a random share of users (E3) and the groups are balanced on device and usage (C1); there is a specific new-library crash mechanism absent from 7.3.2 (C2); and the platform console confirms the gap (C2).
The flag eligibility rule requires capability canvas.tiles.v1, which first shipped in 7.4.0 (E4, C10), so the build determines eligibility by design.
7.3.2 crash rates were unchanged after 9 Sep even though 7.3.2 clients also use zstd (C1, C3), and the steeper overall curve is explained by 7.4.0 adoption (C1).

Turning the flag off would barely change crash rates (C1), the incident would be closed on the wrong cause, and 7.4.0's Pixelda crash (C2) would go to 100% of users, roughly tripling crash rates for everyone still on 7.3.2.
The build, and specifically Pixelda 3.1's HEIF decode crash, drives the gap (C1, C2), so holding the rollout and fixing that cluster addresses the real cause.
A memory-kill effect is plausible (C4, C15) but not yet established in the field (C1 CI −0.02 to +0.20), so requiring a rework now commits ahead of the evidence.

The analyst says widening the holdout would resolve the open flag memory-kill question about a week faster (C1); this is a reasonable way to gather evidence, but it is secondary to fixing the build crash (C2).
Rolling back to Tracewell 4.9 would remove native crash capture and hide the Pixelda SIGSEGV cluster (C2, C11), suppressing information; the console already provides the comparable figures.
The randomized holdout, the version and tier breakdowns (C1) and the cross-validated Pixelda cluster (C2) are enough to commit to holding the rollout and fixing the build (A2).

caseProblems: The presenting request limits collection to two items, but C1 alone settles almost every hypothesis (version split, holdout, device tiers and usage all in one item). It is very decisive and its title signals that it is the confound breakdown.

The numbers are internally consistent: the E1 flag-off rate of 0.74% and the 16 Sep overall rate of 1.01% both reconcile with C1's holdout and 7.3.2 rates. No inconsistency found.
